title: Use native SM100 FA4 forward and backward kernels
body:
Add the `gpu_fa4_cute_sm100` attention backend, which runs upstream FlashAttention-4 (FA4)'s native SM100 forward and backward kernels through Marin's JAX and packed-token mask adapters, and select it in the `moe_hero_ep` hero configuration. It supports BF16, head dimension 128, and GQA ratios 4, 6, and 8 on SM100, and rejects other shapes and hardware.

**Expected hero training-step throughput: about +8%** over `main`'s `gpu_fa4_cute_wide`. This compounds the two paired studies below, each on 64 GB200 GPUs: the native backward (+4.03%) and then the native forward on top of it (+4.02%). No single run compared `main` with the full change.

| Change | Result | Setup |
|---|---|---|
| Native backward vs. previous backward port | **+4.03%** training-step throughput (15.81 → 15.19 s/step, 95% CI 1.42–6.69%) | 64 GB200, 3-pair study stopped after interim results ([protocol and measurements](https://github.com/mcwitt-agent/marin/tree/9cf80aafb65b1b146e9655b3f9d4346e96252ed8/experiments/benchmarks)) |
| Native forward vs. previous forward | **+4.02%** training-step throughput (95% CI 1.11–6.92%) | [3 matched pairs, 64 GB200](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fmwittmann%2Ffa4-forward-e2e-20260921d), 20 measured steps per arm, native backward in both arms |
| Forward tile 128×64 vs. default 128×128 | **2.74 → 2.10 ms** on [packed short documents](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fmwittmann%2Ffa4-tiles-forward-20260922c), **3.25 → 3.58 ms** on [long full-causal documents](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fmwittmann%2Ffa4-tiles-forward-20260922b) | attention microbenchmark; 128×128 kept |

In the forward benchmark, all six runs completed 28 updates with finite losses, and matched-step losses differed by at most 0.00031 nats. On GB200, 18 packed-attention output and gradient parity cases pass for GQA ratios 4, 6, and 8, with changing segment boundaries, padding, and sliding windows ([GPU test](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fmwittmann%2Fep-opt-d768-sm100-gqa6-parity-d-20260922)). The training benchmarks ran on earlier revisions of the adapter code.

Context-sharded queries use #9117's layout: each shard keeps the full K/V, the kernels apply global query offsets, and partial K/V gradients are summed across shards.

`gpu_fa4_cute` keeps its behavior, including the H100/SM90 path, and now shares mask, sparse-metadata, and backward pre/postprocessing code with the new backend. The unused `gpu_fa4_cute_wide` backend is removed.

The native kernels need FA4 4.0.0b27 or newer, which `marin-core[gpu]` and `levanter[gpu]` already require. #9353 raises the `--extra pipeline` environment to the same versions.
